messages:
Maya Patel: FYI support is getting multiple escalations from customers in us-west-2 — lots of 502/504s and timeout reports against the hosted inference API since ~2024-06-12T13:28:00 PDT. Customers report retries and increased token billing.

Maya Patel: sample from customer A: curl "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-open-1\",\"input\":\"hi\"}' --max-time 10
response: 502 Bad Gateway (no body)

Support Bot: +3 customers opened priority tickets. Topline: client-perceived latency spike then 5xx.

Rajesh (neteng): tagging @oncall-bot @Claire Ong. Any infra deploys around 13:25?

deploy-bot: No deploys to prod in the last 60m.

Claire Ong: Confirming — no planned deploys. We see an uptick in gateway 502s in us-west-2 gateway fleet. Rate of 502s up from baseline 0.3% to ~8% starting 13:27 PDT.

Ben Liu: Adding logs from gateway (redacted):
```
2024-06-12T13:28:05Z gateway-uw2-02 ERROR upstream read timeout id=xyz status=502 rt=12004ms
2024-06-12T13:28:06Z gateway-uw2-07 WARN tcp conn reset by peer hop=3
```

Maya Patel: Customers also complaining about auth failures intermittently (401 -> then back to 200 after retry). Could be packet loss causing connection resets to auth service.

Rajesh (neteng): I'm starting network triage. Can someone run an mtr from a failing gateway host to the auth/ingress egress IP and share results? Prefer short-run (100 pings).

Ben Liu: Running from gateway-uw2-02:
```
$ mtr -r -c 100 198.51.100.25
Start: Wed Jun 12 13:29:01 2024
HOST: gateway-uw2-02
 1.|-- 10.0.8.1        0.0%  0.6ms
 2.|-- 203.0.113.5     0.0% 12.1ms
 3.|-- 198.51.100.1    3.0% 25.3ms
 4.|-- 198.51.100.25  18.0% 41.8ms  <-- significant loss
 5.|-- 198.51.200.2    0.0% 45.1ms
```

Rajesh (neteng): hop 4 is a provider hop showing ~18% loss from this vantage. Running traceroutes from multiple gateways now.

Claire Ong: We also see increased retransmits on the egress NIC on a subset of gateway nodes (kernel tcp_retransmits metric up). Not widespread but concentrated in uw2-o (one availability zone).

Maya Patel: Customer impact correlates with uw2-a and uw2-o ingress. Several customers with traffic pinned to those AZs showed the highest error rates.

Rajesh (neteng): I'm seeing BGP path changes in the provider AS for prefixes that carry our egress NAT IPs around 13:26-13:30 PDT. Possible flapping or microloops. Opening ticket with provider now — sending them traceroutes and mtr output.

Rajesh (neteng): Mitigation options: 1) shift egress via alternate provider/peer (we have standby peer) 2) move traffic to other AZs (can be done via routing policy in our edge LB) 3) temporarily raise TCP keepalive/retry thresholds to reduce resets (short-term). Thoughts?

Claire Ong: Let's shift traffic away from the affected AZ first (option 2). That will avoid touching BGP. Rolling traffic to uw2-b/c should be quick via edge LB policy change. Prepare canary then wider.

oncall-bot: @Rajesh, initiating edge LB policy change. Starting canary: 10% to uw2-b/c.

Ben Liu: Canary in progress. Observability: gateway 502 rate dropping from 8% -> 4% on canaried hosts.

Support Bot: Customers on the canaried flows reporting improvement after ~2 minutes.

Rajesh (neteng): Still opening provider ticket but pushing primary traffic shift to avoid customer disruption. Will monitor BGP updates.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift to uw2-b/c at 10% -> 50% -> 100% in 3 waves.

Maya Patel: Noted some billing queries — customers worried about being charged for retries/failures. We should prepare a credit runbook.

Claire Ong: Gateway logs after full shift show 502s back to baseline ~0.4% and auth 401 anomalies resolved. Latency percentiles also improved.

Rajesh (neteng): Provider acknowledged intermittent BGP withdrawal/AS path oscillation. They marked incident as "flapping peer" and applied dampening. They confirm some of our prefixes transited a congested internal link. They patched route reflectors and applied filters. Monitoring their updates — looks stable for last 20m.

Maya Patel: Customer communications: draft message for Support to send —
"We're aware of intermittent API errors and timeouts affecting hosted inference in us-west-2 between 13:25–13:50 PDT. Root cause: upstream transit provider route instability causing packet loss and connection resets. We routed traffic away from the affected AZs and worked with the provider to stabilise routes. Services are recovered; if you still see errors please DM with request IDs. We are evaluating credits for affected customers."

Claire Ong: After mitigation, can we document exact repro steps for SRE and Support for future? I captured steps we used to confirm packet loss:
1) From gateway host: `mtr -r -c 100 <target>` and `traceroute -n <target>`
2) Check kernel tx/rx drops on NIC: `cat /proc/net/netstat && ethtool -S eth0 | grep drop`
3) Compare across AZs to see if loss is AZ-scoped
4) If provider hop shows loss, open provider ticket with mtr/traceroute and BGP update timestamps

Ben Liu: Also add: TTL-limited tcpdump to capture RSTs and retransmits: `tcpdump -i eth0 -n dst host 198.51.100.25 and tcp` and collect 60s sample.

Rajesh (neteng): Follow-ups: provider to confirm root fix, we should 1) add fallback peer for that transit prefix, 2) set automated traffic shift policy for >3% gateway 5xx in AZ for >5m, 3) add alert for provider BGP flaps on our prefixes.

Maya Patel: Support: Please triage tickets with the standard "we mitigated and routed traffic" note and offer credits. Escalate any ongoing 5xx after 14:00 PDT.

oncall-bot: Incident transitioned to "post-incident review". Tagging for postmortem: @Claire Ong (owner), @Rajesh (neteng), @Maya Patel (support).

Claire Ong: Will draft a postmortem with timeline, mitigations, and action items. Preliminary action item: implement automatic AZ failover policy and runbook for provider flaps.

Maya Patel: Thanks team. Closing channel for updates — put final postmortem link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
